status: preregistered after closing the triple-cache OOM and before c96 oracle or candidate measurement
purpose: Measure whether raising pinned concurrency from 64 to 96 increases aggregate decode throughput with the qualified exact ffn_down+ffn_gate F16 cache, without transferring the c64 rate or oracle.
hardware: Two local Intel Arc Pro B70 cards; no remote host.
fixed_configuration: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M, llama.cpp SYCL TP2 tensor 1,1, MTP0, normal MMQ Q4_K reorder, WDC and WDC pre-reorder off, 96 pinned slots, total context 32768, batch 2048, ubatch 256, FUSE_EXT=31, temperature 0, prompt cache off, 128 generated token IDs per request, inference admission target 96 with 1000 ms fail-safe ceiling.
oracle_rule: Run one fresh cache-off control in baseline-generation mode at c96. It is an oracle-generation arm, not a publishable speed point. Freeze its 96 complete token-ID digests and require the cache candidate to match all 96 exactly.
candidate: GGML_SYCL_Q4K_F16_CACHE_FILTER=ffn_down,ffn_gate; cached tensors contain the exact incumbent Q4_K-to-F16 dequantized bytes and use the unchanged GEMM arithmetic.
advance_rule: The cache-off oracle arm must produce 96 complete 128-token rows, zero cached tokens, zero cross-base collisions, and clean health. The first cache candidate must fit, pass 96/96 complete token identity against that frozen oracle, zero cached tokens, zero collisions, cache liveness, clean shutdown and kernel-health gates, and exceed the higher qualified c64 observation of 175.798577 tok/s. Only then run one fresh candidate repeat. Promotion requires both candidates 96/96 and their two-run center above the qualified c64 center of 175.623794 tok/s.
failure_policy: Any oracle-arm failure closes the experiment. An OOM, health failure, output mismatch, or first candidate at or below 175.798577 tok/s closes c96 without a repeat. No baseline-generation, failed-arm, or single-run speed is promoted; no rate transfers to another concurrency, context, quantization, card count, MTP depth, or one-user route.
